text:
irene: Quick follow-up from yesterday's postmortem on the cross-region routing spike — consolidated action items and owners below. I'll keep a running tracker here. TL;DR: oscillating route churn in the LB control plane, intermittent TLS handshakes in region-2, and client-side fallback + retries amplifying the load. Need owners and ETAs.

ops-bot: Postmortem created: PM-2026-042, link: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/PM-2026-042 :spiral_note_pad: 

akash: I'm taking the routing bug. Initial hypothesis: stale canary route rules + sticky DNS TTL shadowing causing asymmetric fanout. Plan: identify offending rule set, roll back canary, and add guardrail to prevent reapplication. ETA: mitigation patch by 2026-06-04 18:00 UTC.

leo: I'll pair w/ akash on validating all regions after rollback and run targeted e2e probes. Also adding a temporary rate limit on cross-region sticky LB reconfigs.

sam: On TLS side — region-2 shows a cert chain inconsistency on the edge (weird sni mismatch under load). I can reproduce locally with the cert rotation job + high simultaneous handshake load. Owning: cert-rotation sanity checks + stronger backoff in the edge handshake path. ETA for fix and rollout: 2026-06-05 12:00 UTC.

maria: I'll own monitoring + alerting follow-ups. Action items: add a dedicated metric for 'edge_tls_handshake_retry' and create a composite alert that includes increased 5xx + handshake_retry spikes. Will add alert runbook. ETA: 2026-06-04 23:00 UTC.

irene: Concrete action list I'm writing down here so we can triage in the sync tomorrow. Please confirm owners or reassign.

- ACTION akash: rollback canary route set + prevent reapply (mitigation) — ETA 2026-06-04 18:00 UTC
- ACTION leo: post-rollback region verification + probe sweep — ETA 2026-06-04 20:00 UTC
- ACTION sam: cert-rotation fix + edge handshake backoff — ETA 2026-06-05 12:00 UTC
- ACTION maria: metrics/alert + runbook update — ETA 2026-06-04 23:00 UTC
- ACTION dev-rel: communicate customer impact windows for Dedicated tenants (short message + link to status page) — ETA 2026-06-04 21:00 UTC

dev-rel: Copy — I can push a short notification and pin the status page. Will coordinate wording with SRE.

akash: Quick note — I'm seeing a secondary pattern where some hosts persisted older route versions in cache for ~90s due to an edge sync race. I'll add a TTL bump + explicit invalidation as part of the mitigation.

leo: For verification, I'll run the probe matrix across us-east/us-west/eu and confirm no cross-region asymmetric responses. Posting probe command here:
```
curl -sSf -H "Host: model.redwood.internal" https://lb-probe.local/ping -I
```

maria: Adding the new alert to the 'networking' channel and attaching a minimal runbook snippet. Runbook excerpt:
"If edge_tls_handshake_retry > 50/min AND 5xx_rate_increase > 0.5% => call SRE oncall, escalate to networking-owners."

irene: Thanks. I'll convert these into JIRA tasks and set up a follow-up sync in 24h. Also adding a recurring check for 'retry amplification' patterns into the incident playbook — this has become a recurring theme.

ops-bot: Reminder: Oncall handoff at 2026-06-05 08:00 UTC.

akash: Update 2026-06-04 17:45 UTC: rollback complete in canary, invalidation pushed, TTL bump staged. Monitoring looks good so far, still watching for residual retries.

leo: Update 2026-06-04 19:30 UTC: region probe sweep completed. No asymmetric routing detected in probe set (us-east/us-west/eu). Posting summary CSV to the postmortem doc.

sam: Update 2026-06-05 11:30 UTC: rolled cert-rotation sanity checks and decreased handshake concurrency for region-2. Early telemetry shows handshake_retry down ~75%. Rolling to remaining edges after lunch.

maria: Update 2026-06-05 12:10 UTC: alert firing rate back to baseline. Runbook updated and linked in PM-2026-042. Closing immediate follow-up tasks and moving residual items to a grooming ticket for next sprint.

irene: Awesome work team. I'll mark this thread as the canonical follow-up and close the loop after the grooming ticket lands. If anything regresses, reopen here and ping @channel. :thumbsup:
